name: The Barrow of the Reed King
region_detail: A low mound amid dense reed beds in the lower marshlands.
site_type: tomb | Ancient sites | Ancient burial mound and sealed stone tomb.
history: Ssaresh tradition holds that a forgotten ruler was buried beneath the mound when the surrounding waterways followed a different course. The burial was sealed with carved stone doors and covered with earth. Later generations preserved accounts of the burial, but the shifting marsh obscured its approaches.
current_state: The mound is surrounded by reeds and shallow pools. Annual floods have exposed fragments of worked stone and small ornaments along its slopes. A portion of a carved doorway is visible during periods of low water, although no recent entry into the tomb is known.
inhabitants: Marsh wildlife and occasional Ssaresh visitors; any inhabitants or guardians of the tomb remain undetermined.
danger_level: Low to moderate on the approach; uncertain within the burial chambers.
points_of_interest:
Reed-covered mound; carved doorway; serpent and crocodile motifs; displaced ornaments; waterlogged approach; possible lower burial chambers.

Unresolved elements: The identity of the buried ruler and the age of the tomb; Whether the burial has remained intact; The significance of the carvings and ornaments; Whether the Ssaresh regard entry as permissible, sacrilegious, or dependent upon particular rites.
discovery: A low mound amid dense reed beds in the lower marshlands. Ssaresh elders preserve competing descriptions of the mound. Comparing their accounts with recovered ornaments or examining flood debris may identify the site.
related_records:
Rumor: R-WB-008 — The Reed King’s Tomb — Direct. The mound and carved stone entrance are the subject of the legend.

Notable individuals and factions: Ishkara Silt-Eye (N-069) — may know accounts of the ruler and the tomb’s customary protections; Tiss of the Nets (N-071) — familiar with local traditions and the significance of recovered ornaments; Ssaresh elders and fishing families.
